subject: Retain PassDoor traversal direction for AI Position
description: `parity-random-save-replays-60s-15x-schema14/traces/Savegame_linux2/Profile_002/Savegame_002/replay-009-session-0001.jsonl.zst` previously diverged after frame 516 because a direct PassDoor movement element retained Rust's default direction `0`. Original defines a gate's `mbDirect` as outside-to-inside (`original-code/RHGate.h:73`); `RHSequence::AppendMoveToSequence` attaches that path-local gate to the PassDoor element (`original-code/RHsequence.cpp:568-570`), and `RHSequenceElementMovement::SetGate` stores `mbDirect` as movement direction 1 or 0 (`original-code/RHSequenceElementMovement.cpp:394-406`). `RHArtificialIntelligence::Position` then resolves a selected PassDoor actor to the gate's inside position when that direction is nonzero and its outside position otherwise (`original-code/RHartificialintelligence.cpp:4307-4324`). Rust's wrong direct value exposed the outside endpoint to the patrol chief, which queued `CALL_PATROL_COORDINATE` and later produced the spurious close-point `EVENT_REACHPOINT` at frame 516. Commit `dc09f516de53692235c89af3615d367473bda197` stores `i16::from(GateShot.direct)` only on the generated PassDoor movement. The focused `gate_builder_retains_direct_pass_direction_for_ai_position` regression passes and verifies both polarities end to end: direct stores 1 and resolves the inside point and sector, while indirect stores 0 and resolves the outside point and sector without falling back to the actor's raw position. The optimized parity-profile build succeeds. The representative clears frame 516 and advances to its pre-existing independent frame-711 path frontier, where Civilian65 queues a path with different goal bits and tolerance (Original 0, Rust 70); it does not match exact EOF. The schema-14 control `parity-random-save-replays-60s-15x-schema14/traces/Savegame_Cyrdach/Profile_156/Savegame_001/replay-009-session-0001.jsonl.zst` matches every recorded frame through exact EOF on the same optimized runner.
